strengths: The problem is well motivated. Figure 1 provides a clear analytical example where both ignoring context and intervening on all controllable variables prevent attainment of the optimal reward.

Combining graph-derived policy scopes with contextual Bayesian optimization is a useful approach to continuous causal decision problems. Removing unnecessary intervention and context variables can substantially reduce optimization dimensionality.

The experiments use 110 seeds, report uncertainty, share the HEBO optimizer across methods, and examine settings where baselines can and cannot attain the optimum. The manuscript also acknowledges a case where CoBO converges faster.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.1 is not established by the supplied proof. Appendix A applies single-GP concentration to the function indexed by i*, although i* is selected as the best among m sampled functions. A simultaneous confidence argument across functions is missing, normally introducing logarithmic dependence on m in the exploration parameter. The stated summability condition on pi_t is also inconsistent with the confidence schedule.

The proposed CoCa-BO algorithm lacks adequate justification for its scope-selection rule. Its MAB-UCB rewards change as the underlying HEBO policies improve. Section 5.2's observation that rewards become stationary at optimality does not justify stationary-bandit confidence bounds during learning. Theorem 4.1 analyzes a different algorithm and does not resolve this issue; decreasing average regret over 700 iterations does not establish asymptotic convergence.

The novelty is limited relative to the cited foundations. POMPS selection comes from prior work, and the method combines it with existing UCB and HEBO components. Multi-function BO can also be formulated as ordinary GP-UCB on a disjoint union of domains with a block-diagonal kernel. The manuscript does not sufficiently establish a substantial theoretical advance beyond this formulation.

The evaluation does not isolate the proposed selection mechanism. There are no comparisons between UCB, uniform allocation, and acquisition-based selection over the same POMPS candidates. In particular, the PSA experiments have only one POMPS, so their improvements cannot validate MAB-based scope selection. The benchmarks are a small collection of constructed SCMs, without broader evidence across graph structures and numbers of candidate scopes.

The benchmark specifications contain material inconsistencies. Appendix B.2 omits Cancer from the PSA equation, although the subsequent derivation requires adding it to obtain the claimed zero optimum. Appendix D defines C4 using itself, contradicting the acyclic model. Appendix E ignores the 0.1 coefficients when calculating target variance. These require correction and verification against the experimental implementation.

Scalability and reproducibility are insufficiently demonstrated. Parallelizing an exponential scope search does not remove its worst-case cost, and no runtime or memory scaling study is provided. The high-dimensional example mainly adds deliberately redundant variables. The manuscript also lacks concrete MAB-UCB configuration details and a code link despite claiming to share an implementation.
